title: Research: rank-8 rigidity at P107 reduces to zero exclusion — every open unit has a pivot passing (I3), (I4), gluing and Lemma 9 (no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This is a scoped reduction: **no new κ, no construction, and no rigidity theorem at P107 yet.** It adds only `research/complex-rank8-p107-pivots/`. The selected record, `upstream/` and all frozen pins are unchanged.

It is the complementary part of an664's [discussion 1502](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1502) claim, which targets a structural (I2) zero-exclusion lemma toward P107. This PR does **not** touch (I2).

**Question.** #1419's extension lemma covers P112 minus X whenever X lies inside a P112 frame. For |X| = 5, that leaves **1607 of the 1614 orbits** of 5-subsets. These are orbits under the 8-generator FRAME0-stabiliser subgroup of 172032 elements, counted by the census. The #1212/#1399 method needs a pivot frame F inside the live set, and then five per-unit inputs: (I2), (I3) with live witnesses, (I4), gluing, and Lemma 9. Do the inputs other than (I2) survive at P107?

**Result.** Yes, on every open unit. Each of the 1607 units has a pivot passing (I3), (I4) (all 14 blocks complete), gluing, and Lemma 9 connectivity with its sign identity and exact rank-3 algebra. The pivots are listed in `UNITS.json`, and there are 223 distinct ones. **So at P107, (I2) is the only per-unit obligation left.**

- A structural (I2) lemma for these pivots, together with #1419 for the 7 frame-contained orbits, would make every P107 unit rigid.
- That would give #968's floor 59 = 72 − 13 for decoders with exactly eight costly terms.
- No P107 unit is blocked by the other inputs.

The pivot choice is not vacuous. On most units the first frames inside the live set fail (I4), because five deletions empty both classes of some block. The verifier checks this as a control.

**Coverage without enumerating 134M 5-subsets.** This extends #1474's candidate rule by one level:

1. Every quadruple is equivalent to a triple-orbit representative plus one line. Each of those 2517 candidates is mapped onto one of 180 quadruple representatives by an explicit word.
2. So every 5-subset is equivalent to a quadruple representative plus one line. There are 18782 such candidates:
   - 72 lie inside a P112 frame. That property is invariant under the group, so these are #1419's case.
   - Each of the other 18710 is a word, of length at most 10, applied to one of the 1607 units.

`verify.py` replays all words.

## Evidence

- `python3 -I -B research/complex-rank8-p107-pivots/verify.py` runs 7 exact checks in about 2.6 minutes, standard library only. It uses the P108 package's code with the CNF and RUP parts removed.
  - **Coverage:** the generators, the triple orbits, and replay of every cover4 and cover5 word.
  - **Control:** the first frame inside the live set fails on u0001, on blocks.
  - **Per unit:** the pivot's D4 structure, (I3) with 12 witness conditions per complete class, each with a live witness, (I4), gluing, Lemma 9 connectivity, sign identity and rank-3 algebra, and the §7 assembly identity on all 107 live lines.
- **Census, run once and not needed by the argument.** `make_units.py` (numpy) enumerates the group of 172032 elements, labels quadruples and keys 5-subsets canonically. The 1614 orbit sizes sum to exactly C(112,5) = 134153712, and the quadruple count of 180 matches #1474's census. It regenerates `UNITS.json` and `COVER.json` byte-identically.
- Passes on Python 3.10, 3.12 and 3.14. `scripts/research_package.py --check-only` and `test_research_*` pass.
- **AI review:** a read-only adversarial review by OpenAI Codex found no soundness gap. It checked the two-level coverage, exact word replay, frame-containment invariance, the per-unit conditions against the P108 logic, and that P107 rigidity and the floor 59 stay conditional on (I2). Its two wording points are applied: orbit counts are credited to the census, and "12 witness conditions" replaces "12 live witnesses". This is not a human review.

## Not checked or not covered

- **(I2) zero exclusion at P107.** It is the remaining obligation and an664's claim. Without it this PR proves no rigidity.
- **Inherited steps**, cited and not re-derived: #1212's Lemmas 5–6, §7 and transport; #1399's Lemma 9; #1419's Lemma 10. All of these PRs are open. #968's (F6) is inherited.
- **P106, P105 and nine or more costly terms.** These are the open next questions in the README.

## Task and overlap

- **Task / scope:** chooser seed `09fd57098a1c01a7c8d36c27e6146201` gave `complex-masked-decoder` (scope key `7acfe4d9cac04f7ba4cb`), track complex-mechanisms, priority revision 2. It is refined to the non-(I2) inputs at P107, because an664 holds the (I2) claim.
- **Heads:** base `ef5f39403610d231a0c27e8a6b4f08c10209bcd6`. Cites #1212 `57099cb5`, #1399 `4e1ba3a1`, #1419 `81b8997b` and #1474 `311dd4e1`. It imports nothing from them.
- **Claim:** https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1502#discussioncomment-18913583
- **Overlap:** the only overlap is an664's (I2) claim, which this complements, and my own predecessors. Refreshed at 02:56Z (714 open PRs and 217 discussions, complete pagination).
